chunks: ʿĀṣim ibn Ḥumayd narrated from Muḥammad ibn Qays, who said:

I said to him: A man bequeathed to another man a bequest from his wealth, a third or a fourth, then the man is killed by mistake, meaning the testator. So he said: "This bequest is to be carried out for him from his wealth and from his blood money (diyyah)."

key_terms.الْمُوصِيَ: the testator, the one who made the bequest
key_terms.دِيَتِهِ: his blood money compensation paid for wrongful killing
key_terms.وَصِيَّةٍ: a bequest or testamentary allocation made from one's estate

ai.seo_question: If a person makes a bequest and is then killed by mistake, is the bequest executed from both his estate and his diyyah?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding a bequest made by a person who is later killed by mistake. It states that the bequest is to be fulfilled not only from the deceased's existing property but also from the diyyah owed for his wrongful death, showing that the blood money is treated as part of the estate for this purpose.
